result: The onset of cortical neurogenesis begins immediately before E12.5, and at this stage most VZ progenitor cells are already neurogenic.
evaluation: Claims C19 and C20 are supported by retroviral labeling experiments showing that ~50% of lineages at E12.5 are one- or two-cell clones, indicating neurogenic divisions. This is consistent with previous reports (Gao et al., 2014) and provides direct experimental evidence for the timing of neurogenesis onset.

result: VZ progenitor cells at E12.5 generate three types of lineages: translaminar (~80%), deep layer-restricted (~10%), and superficial layer-restricted (~10%), as demonstrated by three independent lineage-tracing methods.
evaluation: Claims C21-C23 (retroviral), C25-C27 (MADM), and C28-C30 (genetic fate mapping) provide converging evidence from three independent methods. While individual percentages vary slightly between methods (retroviral: 63% translaminar, 15% deep, 22% superficial; MADM: majority translaminar, ~7% deep, minimal superficial; genetic: ~75% translaminar, ~13% deep, ~11% superficial), the combined analysis (C31) provides a robust estimate. The discrepancy in superficial lineages between MADM and other methods is acknowledged and explained by methodological differences (C58-C60).

result: IPCs at E12.5 exclusively generate one-cell and two-cell clones, including some that produce superficial layer pyramidal cells.
evaluation: Claim C24 is supported by Tbr2CreERT2 lineage tracing showing 73 IPC-derived lineages contained only one or two cells. Claim C68 extends this finding by noting that some IPCs generate superficial layer neurons at E12.5, when deep layer neurons are predominantly being generated, supporting the existence of superficial layer-restricted lineages.

result: Pyramidal cell lineages exhibit diverse laminar configurations, with only about a quarter containing neurons in every cortical layer (II-VI), and clonal sizes following a bimodal distribution with peaks at approximately four and eight cells.
evaluation: Claims C32-C34 are supported by detailed analysis of Emx1-CreERT2;RCL-Gfp lineages shown in Figure 5. The bimodal distribution (C34) is clearly demonstrated and corresponds to laminar-restricted and translaminar lineages respectively. Similar results were obtained with retroviral and MADM methods (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), providing independent validation.

result: Translaminar lineages typically show bias toward superficial layers, with diverse combinations of pyramidal cell subtypes; only a minor fraction contains all three main classes of excitatory projection neurons (CCPN, SCPN, CThPN).
evaluation: Claims C35-C37 and C71-C73 are supported by detailed molecular characterization using Ctip2 and Satb2 markers (Figure 5g-h, Figure 5—figure supplement 2). The finding that nearly a quarter of all-layer translaminar lineages are composed exclusively of CCPNs (C36) and that only a minor fraction contains the entire complement of subtypes (C37, C73) challenges the notion of uniform multipotent progenitors.

result: The heterogeneity in cortical lineages arises directly during neurogenesis, as lineage diversity and proportions are remarkably similar between P2 and P21.
evaluation: Claims C38-C40 are supported by comparison of lineages at P2 and P21 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3). No significant differences were found in clonal size, relative frequency of lineage types, or diversity of lineage patterns, indicating that cell death has minimal impact on lineage heterogeneity. This provides strong evidence that heterogeneity arises during neurogenesis rather than through postnatal refinement.

result: The laminar distribution of neurons within each lineage arises from an organized pattern of neurogenesis rather than random distribution.
evaluation: Claim C41 is supported by permutation analysis (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) showing that randomly permuting neurons while maintaining laminar identities and clonal sizes fails to reproduce the observed anti-correlation between superficial and deep layer neurons. This demonstrates that lineage structure is non-random and reflects organized neurogenic processes.

result: Mathematical modeling demonstrates that a stochastic mechanism with two progenitor populations best reproduces experimental lineage diversity, including bimodal clonal size distribution and laminar configurations.
evaluation: Claims C42-C47 describe Bayesian inference and sequential stochastic modeling results (Figures 6-7). Model 1 (single progenitor type, C43-C45) reproduced most features but failed to capture bimodal clonal size distribution and showed exaggerated anti-correlation. Model 2 (two progenitor populations, C46-C47) faithfully reproduced all experimental features including total laminar fractions, bimodal clonal size distribution, and correlation patterns. Claims C82-C83 provide the mechanistic interpretation. The modeling is rigorous and well-validated against experimental data.

result: Subtle tuning of generation probabilities in the stochastic model can replicate different laminar ratios between cortical areas (S1 vs V1), suggesting that progenitor cells in different areas are constrained by different probabilistic rules.
evaluation: Claims C48-C49 are supported by experimental measurements of laminar differences between S1 and V1 (Figure 7g) and successful in silico replication using Model 2 with adjusted probabilities (Figure 7h). Claims C84-C86 extend this to suggest area-specific probabilistic rules. While the number of lineages per area is acknowledged as insufficient for conclusive evidence (C85), the modeling provides proof-of-principle that the stochastic framework can generate diverse cytoarchitectures.

result: Each lineage-tracing method has specific limitations: retroviral labeling is prone to silencing but unbiased; MADM requires cell division and misses quiescent progenitors; genetic fate-mapping cannot distinguish division types.
evaluation: Claims C55-C61 provide critical methodological assessment. The limitations are well-documented in the literature (C55-C57) or demonstrated by comparing results across methods (C58-C59). The hypothesis that MADM misses quiescent progenitors (C60) is reasonable given the discrepancy in superficial lineages between methods. This multi-method approach with explicit acknowledgment of limitations strengthens the overall conclusions.

result: Previous MADM-based studies failed to identify laminar-restricted lineages and underestimated small clonal sizes; the current study reveals bimodal clonal size distribution and that approximately one in six progenitors generate laminar-restricted lineages.
evaluation: Claims C62-C63 accurately describe limitations of previous work (Gao et al., 2014). Claims C64-C67 present new findings that contradict the previous deterministic model. The bimodal distribution (C64) is clearly demonstrated across multiple methods. The identification of laminar-restricted lineages with all three methods (C66-C67) provides strong evidence against previous conclusions.

result: Progenitor cells generate pyramidal cell lineages with heterogeneous sizes and laminar configurations, challenging the deterministic model of cortical neurogenesis.
evaluation: These claims represent the core experimental finding of the study. Claims C2 and C50 are summary statements supported by the comprehensive lineage-tracing data (C21-C37, C51-C52). Claim C74 synthesizes the variance in clonal size and composition. Claim C75 explicitly challenges the deterministic model of Gao et al. (2014), which is justified by the extensive experimental evidence presented.

result: The stochastic model of cortical neurogenesis represents a robust and adaptable mechanism capable of generating diverse neocortical cytoarchitectures without requiring extensive progenitor heterogeneity.
evaluation: Claims C3-C4 and C53-C54 are high-level conclusions supported by the modeling results (C42-C47, C76). Claim C77 is a key inference that diverse lineages do not require corresponding progenitor heterogeneity, supported by Model 2 requiring only two progenitor types. Claims C89-C90 emphasize the parsimony and robustness of the model. These conclusions are well-supported by the combined experimental and modeling evidence.

result: Some progenitors are tuned to generate superficial layer pyramidal cells from early stages of corticogenesis, and most translaminar lineages arise from progressive divisions of individual progenitor cells.
evaluation: Claim C69 is supported by the identification of IPCs at E12.5 generating superficial layer neurons (C68) and is consistent with the existence of superficial layer-restricted lineages. Claim C70 is supported by MADM data showing that symmetric divisions at E12.5 generate at least one translaminar sub-lineage in 58/59 cases. Both claims are well-supported by experimental evidence.

result: The stochastic model is reminiscent of retinal development, where stochastic mechanisms explain most but not all neuronal types; previous studies show limited molecular heterogeneity among VZ progenitors despite morphological differences.
evaluation: Claims C78-C81 provide context from prior work. The comparison to retinal development (C78-C79) is appropriate and supported by citations. Claims C80-C81 accurately represent the literature on progenitor heterogeneity. These claims support the plausibility of the stochastic model but do not constitute primary findings of this study.

result: Stochastic neurogenic decisions likely depend on extrinsic and intrinsic signals affecting cell cycle length, asymmetric inheritance, and other parameters; local signals could tune progenitor behavior across cortical areas without requiring region-specific progenitor populations.
evaluation: Claims C87-C88 are speculative mechanistic proposals supported by citations to relevant literature (C87) but not directly tested in this study. While the modeling demonstrates that different probabilistic rules can generate area-specific cytoarchitectures (C49), the actual molecular mechanisms remain unknown. These are reasonable hypotheses for future work but lack direct experimental support in the current study.

result: Background knowledge and prior work establish that the neocortex contains diverse pyramidal cell types with distinct cytoarchitectures, generated from RGCs through symmetric and asymmetric divisions, with debate over whether progenitors are multipotent or fate-restricted.
evaluation: Claims C1 and C5-C17 establish the scientific context and prior work. These are accurately represented and appropriately cited. They provide essential background for understanding the significance of the current findings but do not constitute results of this study.

result: Retroviral infection labels only one of two daughter cells from a progenitor division due to single-copy integration.
evaluation: Claim C18 describes the mechanism of retroviral labeling, which is established knowledge and correctly applied to interpret the experimental results. This is a methodological detail rather than a primary finding.
